hook.text: Breakfast cereals, pasta, pet food, and plant-based meat alternatives all come from the same machine—the food extruder.

buildup.text: An extruder forces dough through a heated barrel using rotating screws. High temperature (150–200°C) and pressure (30–60 bar).

discovery.text: As the dough exits through a die, sudden pressure drop causes water to flash into steam—puffing the product.

twist.text: Extrusion can texturize plant protein to mimic meat fibers.

climax.text: Extrusion Cooking matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Cook, mix, shape, and puff—all in one machine.

quiz.question: How do puffed cereals get their puffy texture?
options: Sudden pressure drop causes water to flash into steam as dough exits the extruder
